verdict.rationale: Logseq's documented linking primitives — page/block references ([[ ]], (( ))) and simple queries ({{query}}) — provide the backbone for connecting and filtering notes, and the Whiteboard feature offers a spatial canvas with connectors for arranging knowledge visually, but no evidence explicitly documents a dedicated interactive 'graph view' with node-link visualization or filtering controls. Community reports also note serious performance degradation ('indexing and general responsiveness slows down massively once you have a few million words') which would hamper exploring a large graph. missing for 10: explicit documentation of the graph-view visualization UI and its filtering options, and independent confirmation that graph exploration performs well at scale.
